Lost touch with reality? I don't... I mean, I don't think so? It feels real to me. The voice, the drive, all of it. I don't feel like I'm floating away or anything. But I guess reality is sort of subjective, right? 

Like, take photography. I got really obsessed with large-format film photography a while back. I bought this massive 8x10 wooden field camera, the kind where you have to put a dark cloth over your head just to see the ground glass to focus. You don't just snap a picture; you have to calculate the exposure using the Zone System, figuring out exactly how you want the shadows and highlights to fall on the negative. And then you have to develop the sheet film in total darkness. I was using this developer called Pyrocat-HD, which actually stains the film emulsion and gives you these incredibly sharp, contrasty negatives that are perfect for platinum/palladium printing. High? I mean, at first I felt almost lit up, like I had this incredible, urgent purpose that no one else could see. It was amazing. But the flip side was that I would just snap into absolute rage if anyone questioned me or tried to slow me down. I had zero patience for anyone operating at a normal speed.

You can't just buy original replacements, so I spent days carefully desoldering all six chips from the printed circuit board. You have to be incredibly precise, using a specialized vacuum desoldering pump, because if you apply too much heat with the iron, you'll lift the copper traces right off the board and permanently ruin the whole voice architecture. Then I had to soak the chips in a pure acetone bath in a glass jar for exactly 48 hours to dissolve that resin without eating into the silicon. I actually built a makeshift ventilation hood in my dining room just to deal with the fumes. And calibrating it afterward is a nightmare—you have to hook it up to a digital oscilloscope and adjust these tiny trimpots on the motherboard to make sure the pulse width modulation and the filter resonance are perfectly in phase across all six voices. If even one is off by a fraction of a volt, the chords sound completely muddy and out of tune...

Sad? Hopeless? Um... I don't know if I'd use those exact words. It's more like this crushing weight, this absolute void where everything used to be. It's not just a feeling, it's like a physical pressure in the room.

Unstoppable? Invincible? No, I wouldn't say that. I didn't feel like a superhero or anything, just... really, really capable. Like my brain was finally firing on all cylinders and I could just see how everything connected.
